memory_candidates.content: bash's `x="$(some_function ...)"` command-substitution form always forks a subshell, even when `some_function` is defined in a merely-SOURCED (not subshelled) library file. Any global variable that function assigns (e.g. an HTTP-status side-channel like sapience-api-lib.sh's `sapience_api_post_http_status`) is set inside that subshell and is LOST the instant it exits -- it never reaches the caller's shell, regardless of what the library's own header comment claims about being 'sourced, not subshelled' (that claim is true of the library file, not of how a particular call site invokes it). The fix: redirect the function's stdout to a temp file instead of capturing via `$(...)` -- a plain output redirection on a function call does NOT fork a subshell in bash, so globals it sets propagate normally. Verified empirically with a minimal repro. Any new consumer of sapience-api-lib.sh's sapience_post that needs the HTTP status afterward must use this redirect-to-tempfile pattern, never `$(sapience_post ...)`.

bash redirection order matters and silently discards output the wrong way around: `cmd 2>/dev/null >&2` first points fd2 at /dev/null, THEN dups fd1 from fd2's now-redirected target -- so BOTH streams end up discarded, not just the intended stderr-suppression. The correct order to 'send cmd's stdout to the real stderr while suppressing cmd's own stderr' is `cmd >&2 2>/dev/null` (dup fd1 from the still-live fd2 first, then redirect fd2 away). Caught only because a test case asserted the expected diagnostic text actually appeared in captured output; a weaker test (checking only exit code) would have missed this silently.

When a shell test suite drives a PATH-shadowed `curl` stub via env vars to inject fixture responses, those env var NAMES must never collide with a flag name the script-under-test itself parses into an identically-named shell variable (e.g. a test using `DM_BODY=... bash script.sh dm --body "real text"` when the script's own flag parser also assigns `DM_BODY="real text"` from `--body`). The script's own assignment silently overwrites the exported fixture value in that process's environment before the curl stub subprocess ever inherits it, producing a confusing failure where the stub echoes back the CLI argument text instead of the intended fixture body. Prefix stub-driving env vars distinctively (e.g. `STUB_*`) to avoid this collision class entirely, rather than relying on guessing which internal variable names a script under test might use.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience_post HTTP status subshell loss
sapience_notes.value: sapience-api-lib.sh's sapience_post sets sapience_api_post_http_status via a global assignment documented as propagating to the caller's shell, but that guarantee breaks for the idiomatic call pattern x="$(sapience_post ...)" because command substitution always forks a subshell regardless of how the function is defined -- the status is silently lost. Fixed locally in sapience-publish.sh via a redirect-to-tempfile wrapper; not fixed upstream in the shared library (out of file_scope).

sapience_notes.subject: bash redirection order pitfall
sapience_notes.value: cmd 2>/dev/null >&2 discards BOTH stdout and stderr (redirections apply left-to-right: fd2 is redirected to /dev/null first, then fd1 is dup'd from that already-redirected fd2). The correct form to send stdout to the real stderr while suppressing the command's own stderr is cmd >&2 2>/dev/null.

sapience_notes.subject: sapience ko subcommand project-key resolution
sapience_notes.value: sapience-publish.sh's ko subcommand resolves a repo-tagged KO's project key at runtime: --project override wins, else .sapience/project.json's .project cid is matched against GET /v1/people/projects entries' .cid/.id field to recover .key, refusing loudly (no POST) on no binding or no match. The .key field name was not live-reprobed during implementation (same caveat the governing plan already carried at plan time); only stub-fixture-tested.

sapience_notes.subject: doc-version base_rev JSON type handling
sapience_notes.value: The Sapience server's doc rev field's JSON type (numeric counter vs. opaque string token) was never live-reprobed. sapience-publish.sh's doc-version subcommand coerces base_rev via jq's (try tonumber catch $v) so the payload sends a JSON number when the fetched value parses as one, else a JSON string -- correct either way without needing to know the server's actual convention.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience write-surface publishers now exist
sapience_notes.value: agent-system/extensions/sapience/scripts/sapience-publish.sh provides four dry-run-by-default, --confirm-gated write subcommands (doc-comment, doc-version, dm, ko), each with loud-failure handling written against its own endpoint's verified response shape, as the sole prescribed write path for these four surfaces (no MCP write tool is named). This closes the gap the /sapience command's future approval picker needs filled before it can call any concrete publisher.
